1.why: The game exploration/FINDINGS.md was written against. Clean on every invariant, so it is the baseline that proves a failure elsewhere is the data and not the reader.

23.defect: phantom event - statistic credited to an off-court player
23.why: One of the 7 games carrying a misattributed row. No other defect, so it isolates attribution from everything else.

35.why: An overtime game whose tip-off substitutions are mistimed by exactly 60 seconds. This is the case the correction was built for, so it is the test that the correction still helps.

43.defect: minute mismatch the +-60 correction cannot repair - quarantined
43.why: Mismatches by 60 seconds but has no overtime, so the correction rule cannot reach it. One of the two games that stay quarantined. Proves the correction is narrow rather than a blanket 60-second nudge.

75.why: Overtime that reconciles perfectly. Guards the opposite error from game 107: a period rule that invents problems in ordinary overtime.

98.defect: minute mismatch the +-60 correction cannot repair - quarantined
98.why: The second of the two permanently quarantined games. Same shape as 43.

107.why: The only double-overtime game in E2024. ExtraTime is a single JSON list holding every overtime period, so the period boundary has to be counted off the end-of-period markers. A game with one overtime cannot detect an off-by-one in that rule; this one can.

131.defect: overlapping substitution batch plus an off-court attribution
131.why: The only game in the season where the naive batch rule leaves a team showing four players: two Real Madrid events stamped 08:00 land inside a Zalgiris batch stamped 07:12. The absorbing batch rule removes those violations. The same source payload also credits event 168 to P002329 before his IN row, so the permanent result correctly retains one attribution issue.

323.defect: phantom event plus a full 60-second backwards clock step
323.why: Carries both an attribution defect and the largest backwards clock step observed. Two defects in one game is the case where a fix for one can quietly break the other.
